questions.history: Call getNextEntry(), then read the sparse member through end of entry.
questions.prediction: The parent’s extra-record skip predicts lost data or a read failure. On the merge expect exactly three zero bytes followed by ABCD.
questions.basis: Expanding a four-byte extent at logical offset 3 produces those seven bytes. No physical padding lies after an exactly full map record.
questions.refutation: An exception, a missing hole or payload byte, or padding appearing in the logical output on the merge.

questions.history: Encode the same extent with the short decimal map and zero-pad the rest of its 512-byte record.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should extract the identical seven bytes.
questions.basis: The numeric extent and payload are unchanged. Both padding calculations consume the remaining bytes of a partially used record.
questions.refutation: The ordinary short map changes the recovered data or its length on either revision.

questions.history: Keep the aligned map fixed, change only the four stored bytes to WXYZ and continue to the second member.
questions.prediction: On the merge the first readback must become three zeros then WXYZ. The next entry must still be tail with its one byte Z and then the archive must end.
questions.basis: The file data and the next member have independent TAR boundaries. Successful delivery of the first file alone does not prove subsequent alignment.
questions.refutation: The new data is ignored, or the second name, payload or end-of-archive changes.
